title: Indexing rows in a flat map
statement: Let $L$ be a finite list over a type $\alpha$, let $f$ map each element to a Boolean list, and suppose every list $f(a)$ has length $k$. For $i<|L|$ and $j<k$, the element at index $ik+j$ of the concatenation of the lists $f(a)$ for $a$ in $L$, using false as the default when out of range, equals the element at index $j$ of $f(L_i)$ with the same default.
